transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I just don’t care about much anymore. Stuff I used to look forward to, it’s like it’s all gone flat. My fishing gear’s been sitting in the garage untouched, and I used to be real particular about keeping it organized—had these little bins for lures and everything. Now I walk past it and don’t even bother.

Same with the woodshop. I used to lose hours out there, but now it just feels like another chore. Even my kids try to get me to play chess with them, and I’ll sit there, but I’m not really in it. Just kind of moving the pieces because they asked.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About… a year and a half? No, closer to a year and seven months, I think. It started after my wife’s health problems really changed everything at home. Since then it’s just been… hard to get myself back to caring about things.
Do you still enjoy things you used to enjoy, or has the pleasure gone away?

Yeah… the pleasure’s pretty much gone. I mean, I used to get real excited about fishing—checking my tackle, making sure everything was sorted just right, even just messing with the gear in the garage. Now it’s all just sitting there, and I walk by like it belongs to someone else.

And the woodshop too… I used to spend hours out there. Made a bookshelf once that my neighbor still talks about, actually—he keeps saying I should build him another one, but I just… I don’t know. It feels like work now, like something I’m supposed to do instead of something I want to do.

Even with the kids and chess, I’ll sit down because they ask me to, but I’m not really enjoying it. I’m just moving pieces around, waiting for it to be over, which makes me feel awful saying out loud.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad, exactly. I mean… maybe sometimes, but it’s hard for me to put a name on it. It’s more like I’m just there, if that makes sense.

Like at work, when we’re going over plans, I can still point out where something’s off—old habit, I guess. I’ve been doing construction long enough that certain things just jump out at me. But as far as feeling sad most of the time… I don’t know. I haven’t really been keeping track of it that way.
Do you still find any activities or things that give you pleasure?

Not really, no. I mean… I keep trying to think of something, but mostly I just stopped caring about the stuff I used to look forward to.

My fishing gear’s still sitting out in the garage untouched, and that used to be a whole thing for me—getting everything ready, checking lures, all that. The woodshop too… I go out there and it just feels like another chore, like cleaning gutters or something. And even when my kids ask me to play chess, I’ll do it, but I’m mostly just moving the pieces because they want me there. I’m not really… getting anything out of it.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?

I don’t know… “hopeless” is a strong word, I guess. I haven’t really sat down and thought about the future like that.

I mean, with construction you’re always planning ahead—permits, crews, materials, weather messing everything up. There’s this one site where the delivery schedule got all out of order and I spent half the day just trying to get people to stop blaming each other and look at the actual problem. So I can still do that, think a few steps ahead when I have to.

But as far as my own future… I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear answer for that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past year?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I haven’t been weighing myself every day or anything, but my belt’s definitely had to come in a couple notches, and I wasn’t trying to lose weight.

Food just doesn’t really… taste right most days. Like cardboard, kind of. I’ll skip breakfast without even thinking about it, then be out on a job site all day, and by dinner I’m just picking at whatever’s there. My wife will say something about it, and I’ll say I ate earlier, but half the time I didn’t really. 

So yeah, I guess I have lost some. Not like I planned it.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself talking slower, exactly. I mean, on job sites people are always rushing anyway, radios going, somebody asking where the lift is, somebody else looking for plans that should’ve been in the trailer… so I don’t know that I’d catch it.

Moving slower… maybe some mornings I take longer to get going, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean. Nobody’s told me I’m dragging or anything. Are you asking if other people have noticed it, or if I feel it myself?
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to?

I don’t know… slower how, exactly? Like walking across the room, or just getting through the day?

I mean, at work I still get from one end of the site to the other when somebody needs me. Though sometimes I’ll stop because someone left a stack of lumber right where it shouldn’t be, and then I’m dealing with that, and then the electrician wants an answer, and by then I’ve forgotten what I was walking over there for in the first place.

So… I can’t really say I’ve noticed myself moving slower. Maybe I’m not paying attention to it.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

Yeah… all the time, honestly. I mean, I don’t know if “guilty” is even the right word, but it feels like I’m always the one who screwed something up.

Like if one of the kids misses something, or my wife has to pick up slack at home, I start thinking, well, that’s because I’m not doing what I’m supposed to. And at work, if there’s a cost overrun or somebody misses an appointment, or even a safety thing that maybe wasn’t directly my fault, I still take it like… there it is, proof I’m useless.

I’ll get stuck on it. Like everyone would be better off if I wasn’t the one in charge. Then I’ll think about some job from years ago where the concrete truck was late and we had half the crew standing around, and I can still feel my stomach drop like it’s happening now. It’s stupid, I know, but yeah… I feel guilty a lot.
Have you ever thought about ending your life?

I… yeah. I mean, I don’t like saying that out loud.

It’s not like I’m sitting there with some big plan written down or anything, but on those early drives to work, before anybody else is awake and the roads are empty, I’ll catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t make it there. And then sometimes I think about the truck, about just… steering off, and it scares me because it feels too close.

Then I’ll get to the site and someone’s asking about concrete or permits or whatever, and I just shove it down because there’s always something needing an answer. But yeah… I have thought about it.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns over the past year?

Yeah… sleep’s been a mess.

I’ll be completely worn out, like I can barely get myself into bed, and then the second I’m there my head starts going. Bills, schedules, who’s supposed to be where tomorrow, whether I forgot to call somebody back… stupid little things too, like a delivery time or some invoice I’m not even sure is due yet.

Or I’ll fall asleep for a bit and then wake up around three, maybe four in the morning, and that’s it. I just lie there staring at the ceiling until it’s time to get up and drive to the site. Sometimes I tell myself I might as well get going early, but then I’m just sitting there in the truck before anyone else shows up. So… yeah, it’s changed. I don’t really sleep right anymore.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is getting worse over time?

Yeah… I think it is getting worse. It’s like I just stopped caring about the things I used to actually look forward to.

I’ve got fishing gear sitting in the garage, and I used to be real particular about keeping it ready—lines, lures, all that. Now I walk past it and just think, yeah, maybe another time. Same with the woodshop. I used to like making things, fixing little stuff around the house, and now even going in there feels like another job I’m behind on.

And the kids, they’ll ask me to play chess sometimes, and I’ll sit there with them, but I’m not really in it. I’m moving the pieces, trying to seem normal, but I’m just… going through the motions. So yeah, I’d say it’s been getting worse.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the time?

Yeah… most of the time, I guess. It’s like the volume got turned down on everything.

I mean, I’ve got my fishing gear sitting in the garage, and I used to mess with that stuff all the time—checking the line, organizing lures, planning where I’d go when I had a free Saturday. Now it just sits there. I walk past it and think I should do something with it, but I don’t.

Same with the woodshop. I used to enjoy being out there, making something or fixing whatever needed fixing, but now it feels like another chore on a list. And even when my kids ask me to play chess, I’ll sit down with them, but I’m not really… there. I’m moving pieces and trying to act normal, but I’m just going through the motions.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure almost all the time?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. Almost all the time, it feels like I’m just not getting anything out of things anymore.

Like I said, the fishing stuff is still sitting out in the garage, untouched. I used to be the guy who’d have everything organized, you know, and now I’ll see it and just keep walking. Same with the woodshop—used to be where I’d go to clear my head, and now it feels like one more thing I’m supposed to deal with.

Even with my kids playing chess… I sit there, and I love them, obviously, but I’m not really enjoying it. I’m just moving the pieces and trying to look like I’m present. So yeah, it’s pretty much most of the time.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure at all?

Not at all, exactly… I mean, I don’t know if “at all” is the right way to say it. It’s more like I just stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to.

My fishing gear is still sitting untouched in the garage, and I used to be the kind of guy who’d fuss over all that—make sure everything was ready. Now I just walk by it. And the woodshop… that used to be where I’d go to feel useful, I guess, and now it just feels like another chore.

Even with my kids, when they ask me to play chess, I’ll do it, but I’m not really enjoying it. I’m just moving the pieces and trying to seem like I’m there. So… maybe not “at all,” but it’s close enough that it feels that way most of the time.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure at all, or is it just most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d say at all, like literally nothing ever… but it’s most of the time, yeah. I guess the main thing is I just stopped caring about the stuff I used to look forward to.

Like my fishing gear’s still sitting in the garage untouched, and every time I see it I think, “I should really clean that up,” but then I just keep walking. And the woodshop too—I used to spend hours out there, you know, fixing things, making little shelves, whatever needed doing. Now it feels like one more chore, like taking out the trash or something.

Even when the kids ask me to play chess, I’ll sit there and do it, but I’m not really in it. I’m moving the pieces, nodding along… just trying to go through the motions so they don’t notice too much. So, yeah, I guess it’s not every single second, but it’s close. Mostly I just don’t feel much from things anymore.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities and inability to experience pleasure are significantly interfering with your daily life?

Yeah… it is. I mean, I kept telling myself it was just a rough patch or work stress, because construction’s always got something going sideways—permits, subs not showing up, concrete guys arguing with the framers, all that stuff.

But I’ve started missing things at work. Not just little paperwork stuff, but things that could mess with deadlines, or worse, safety. And after that near-miss, I couldn’t really keep pretending it wasn’t affecting anything.

At home, I’m there… like, I’m in the room, I come home, I sit at dinner. But my wife and the kids, they’re kind of having to work around me now. I used to be someone they could count on, and lately it feels like I’m just… taking up space. So yeah, it’s interfering. More than I wanted to admit.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities and inability to experience pleasure have lasted for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… most of the day, I’d say. Nearly every day too, if I’m being honest.

It’s not like I wake up and decide, “I’m not going to care about anything today.” It’s just there. Like I’ll pass my fishing gear in the garage—still sitting there, same as it’s been—and I used to be real particular about that stuff, you know, cleaning it, organizing the tackle box. Now I just look at it and keep walking.

Same with the woodshop. I used to lose track of time out there, and now it feels like another thing I’m supposed to deal with. And the kids’ll ask me to play chess, and I’ll sit down with them, but I’m mostly just going through the motions. Moving pieces, pretending I’m more into it than I am.

So… yeah. It’s there most of the day. It doesn’t really let up much.
Do you feel like your symptoms are severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

Yeah… I think it is. I mean, “severely” sounds like a big word, but… yeah, it’s gotten to that point.

At work I’ve started missing things I really shouldn’t miss. Not just, you know, forgetting to return a call or misplacing a form—stuff that can affect deadlines, and honestly, safety. In construction you can’t be half-there. One thing gets overlooked and suddenly everybody’s scrambling, or worse. After that near-miss, I couldn’t keep telling myself it was just normal stress.

And at home… I’m there, technically. I come in, I sit down, I’m around. But my wife and the kids are kind of having to work around me now, like I’m not someone they can lean on the same way. I used to be the guy who handled things, kept things moving. Lately I feel more like furniture in the room than a husband or a dad. So… yeah, it’s impairing things pretty badly.
